dossier.title: 123rd Air Control Squadron — Blue Ash ANGS

rows.label: Status [D]
rows.text: Active and verified. Provides command, control, and communications worldwide. ~300 Airmen returned from deployment in Dec 2025. Has occupied Blue Ash Air National Guard Station since Nov 1953; marked its 75th anniversary in 2023.

rows.label: The finding
rows.text: The 123rd ACS is a unit of the 178th Wing. The wing whose intelligence group supports NASIC also fields a squadron roughly 15 mi from downtown Cincinnati — the corridor’s southernmost military node. Air Force and National Guard releases consistently refer to "the 178th Wing’s 123rd Air Control Squadron."

rows.label: Scope limit
rows.text: Its mission is C2 / air battle management, not intelligence — it does no NASIC analytic work. Its significance here is geographic: it extends the 178th’s footprint to the Cincinnati metro.

rows.label: Also
rows.text: Hosts recurring combined training with NATO allies (Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Hungary). Blue Ash ANGS was estimated at ~$20M/yr local economic contribution as of 2016.

dossier.sources: nationalguard.mil · ang.af.mil · DVIDS · Blue Ash ANGS

dossier.title: 178th Wing — Springfield-Beckley ANG Base

rows.label: Mission
rows.text: "Ready units to conduct intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and operational support" — MQ-9 Reaper remote ops + an intelligence group. 926 personnel assigned at Springfield ANGB.

rows.label: Structure [D]
rows.text: Four groups. The 178th ISR Group (established 1 Jul 2014) comprises the 124th, 125th, 126th, and 127th Intelligence Squadrons at Springfield.

rows.label: NASIC bridge [D]
rows.text: The intelligence component is Ohio ANG administratively while operationally controlled by the AF ISR enterprise and directly supporting NASIC. A former wing commander is on record describing the 178th ISRG as working closely with NASIC at Wright-Patterson.

rows.label: Cincinnati reach [D]
rows.text: The wing’s 123rd Air Control Squadron sits at Blue Ash ANGS, ~15 mi from downtown Cincinnati (see G-02). C2 mission, not intelligence — the wing’s southernmost unit.

rows.label: Partnerships [D]
rows.text: 2025 releases cite work with NGA, AFRL, Ohio DOT, and the Ohio UAS Center, plus counter-UAS testing during exercise Advanced Wrath.

rows.label: Workforce note
rows.text: A documented Guard→NASIC pathway; ANG commissioning carries government-sponsored TS/SCI as a function of accession.

dossier.sources: ong.ohio.gov · 178wing.ang.af.mil fact sheet · Dayton Daily News · ONG press releases

dossier.title: NASIC — National Air & Space Intelligence Center

rows.label: Mission
rows.text: DoD’s primary source for foreign air and space threats; S&T intelligence lineage (Foreign Technology Division). Air, space, missile, and cyber threat characterization.

rows.label: Scale
rows.text: ~4,100 personnel · budget >$507M · 4 intel groups (Air & Cyberspace / Geospatial & Signatures / Global Exploitation / Space, Missiles & Forces) · 18 squadrons.

rows.label: Location
rows.text: WPAFB Area A, Bldg 856 complex (verified 39.8004°N, 84.0494°W); Foreign Materiel Exploitation incl. Haynes Hall ($29.5M, 58k sq ft). Unit at Springfield ANG Base.

rows.label: Crypto note
rows.text: No public economic/financial-intelligence mission. Do not pitch NASIC as a crypto customer — DoD’s documented crypto demand runs through DARPA/DIA/LE channels and Air Force-awarded analytics subscriptions performed in Tampa, FL (six awards, $7.7M, 2018–2025), none in Dayton.

rows.label: Hiring
rows.text: DCIPS civilian hires sponsor TS/SCI ("able/willing to obtain"). Backgrounds incl. poli-sci, economics, languages, prior military.

rows.label: Mission
rows.text: Space Force intelligence field operating agency — space/counterspace system analysis.

rows.label: History
rows.text: Activated 24 Jun 2022 from NASIC’s space & counterspace squadrons; now ~4 space analysis squadrons.

rows.label: Why it matters
rows.text: Second, growing intelligence employer on the same base with the same contractor-support model.

rows.label: Mission
rows.text: DAF primary S&T center. ~$7B S&T portfolio, 12,000+ employees enterprise-wide.

rows.label: At WPAFB
rows.text: HQ + Aerospace Systems (RQ), Sensors (RY), Materials & Mfg (RX), 711th Human Performance Wing (verified at 39.7908°N, 84.0985°W). [V: confirm current lay-down]

rows.label: Entry doors
rows.text: Strategic Partnering Directorate (2023, one-stop shop) · 2,250+ active partnership agreements · Wright Dialogue with Industry Jul 27–31 2026, Dayton Convention Center · WBI’s AFRL Small Business Hub downtown (N-02).

rows.label: Targeting caveat [D]
rows.text: Confirmed: AFRL’s Information Directorate (AFRL/RI) — the C4I and cyber S&T organization — sits at the Rome Research Site, 525 Brooks Rd, Rome, NY, with 700+ civilian scientists and engineers. It is not resident at WPAFB. Do not assume the crypto-relevant AFRL customer is local; reps attend WDI, so pitch them there.

rows.label: Research signal [D]
rows.text: AFRL/RI publishes research topics on Publicly Available Information (PAI) collection — secure, scalable OSINT retrieval that protects analyst identity and intent — a named, funded research interest.

dossier.title: Air Force Institute of Technology

rows.label: Mission
rows.text: DAF graduate school of engineering & management; professional continuing education for the acquisition and intel workforce.

rows.label: Who can enroll
rows.text: Documented: military (all branches), DoD civilians, DoD contractors, critical-infrastructure employees and sponsored international officers. Unaffiliated applicants can be reviewed but not admitted. Certificates need no GRE/GMAT; $434 per credit hour unless fully sponsored (2026–27).

rows.label: Verify
rows.text: Guard and Reserve eligibility is implied by “US military (all branches)”, not stated (Watchlist vq-afit).

dossier.title: 655th ISR Wing (Air Force Reserve)

rows.label: Mission
rows.text: AFRC’s only ISR wing. Provides ISR capabilities for Air Combat Command, NASIC, and AFMC. Headquartered at Wright-Patterson — on the same installation as NASIC.

rows.label: Scale
rows.text: More than 1,100 military and civilian personnel — Active Guard and Reserve, Air Reserve Technicians, and Traditional Reservists. Under 10th Air Force. Two groups (655th ISRG at WPAFB, 755th ISRG at JB Langley-Eustis), 14 squadrons across 7 states, 10 intelligence missions.

rows.label: At WPAFB
rows.text:
14th IS (acquisitions) — ensures intelligence supportability and provides ISR expertise supporting materiel lifecycle management; active-duty partnership with the 21st IS, part of AFLCMC.
64th IS (HUMINT) — predictive human intelligence collection; directly supports NASIC’s Global Exploitation Group.
The 655th ISRG comprises seven squadrons in total; the 71st IS (GEOINT/MASINT) supports NASIC’s Geospatial & Signatures Intelligence Group from Fort Meade, MD, not co-located here.

rows.label: Why it matters
rows.text: The 14th IS is the corridor’s only published acquisition-intelligence mission — intelligence supportability for materiel lifecycle decisions. The 64th IS is the direct NASIC tie. Both drill at WPAFB itself.

rows.label: Classic associate model
rows.text: Reserve squadrons are embedded with, and work daily alongside, their active-duty counterparts. That is the mechanism by which a part-time Reservist ends up inside NASIC and AFLCMC work.

rows.label: Component note
rows.text: Reserve, not Guard. No state mission; reports through 10th Air Force / AFRC — a structurally different accession path than the ANG’s.

dossier.sources: 445aw.afrc.af.mil (655th ISRW + 655th ISRG official pages, fetched Jul 2026) · AFRC news · collaborationdayton.org
